blocks.text: Every laboratory must have a first aid box. Common accidents and their first aid treatments are given in the Table 16.1 below:

blocks.caption: Table 16.1 Accidents and their First Aid treatment
rows: 1 Cuts
Minor cuts
Remove the glass piece if any, apply a little methylated spirit or tincture iodine with a piece of cotton. Both act as disinfectant.
Serious cuts
Apply pressure on the cut for about 10 minutes to stop bleeding. Consult a doctor.
2 Eye Injuries
Acid in the eye
Wash thoroughly with water and then with 1% sodium bicarbonate solution.
Alkali in the eye
Wash with water followed by 1% boric acid solution.
Foreign particle in the eye
Do not rub the eyes. Remove the particle carefully with soft handkerchief then wash with water.
Soreness in the eye
Put a drop of olive oil in the eyes and keep them closed for some time.
3 Burns
Burns with dry heat (flame, hot object); Burns causing blisters; Acid burns; Alkali burns; Bromine burns

• Apply burnol or mustard oil. • Wash freely with ice cold water. Then wash with a saturated solution of sodium bicarbonate and again with water. • Wash freely with water and then with 1% acetic acid solution and again with water, dry the skin and apply the burnol. • Wash fully with 2% ammonia solution and apply glycerin. Wipe off glycerin after sometime and apply burnol.
4 Poisons
Poisons swallowed
Spit immediately, wash mouth with water repeatedly.
Acid swallowed
Drink a lot of water or lime water or milk of magnesia.
Caustic alkalies swallowed
Drink a lot of water; drink a glass of lemon or orange juice.
Salt of heavy metals swallowed.
Take milk or white part of the egg.
5 Fire
i) Clothes catch fire
Do not run. Wrap with blanket or with dry cotton cloth. Lie down on the floor.
ii) Beaker containing inflammable liquid. catches fire.
Cover the beaker with a duster or damp cloth. This will cut off the supply of oxygen.
iii) Spirit or oil catches fire.
Throw a mixture of sand and sodium bicarbonate. Do not throw water. It will simply spread the fire.
iv) Electric parts catch fire.
Switch off the electric supply immediately and throw sand. Do not throw water in such cases to extinguish fire.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Table 16.1 lists five kinds of burns but prints only four treatments, so the burns cannot be matched line by line. An acid burn is neutralised with a weak base and an alkali burn with a weak acid. The matching is: burns with dry heat: apply burnol or mustard oil; acid burns: wash with ice cold water, then with saturated sodium bicarbonate solution and again with water; alkali burns: wash with water, then 1% acetic acid solution, again water, dry the skin and apply burnol; bromine burns: wash with 2% ammonia solution and apply glycerin, then burnol. No separate treatment is printed for burns causing blisters.
